article.name: Engram Format
article.summary: Engram Format is the open Rust crate and specification for an encrypted SQLite vault and encrypted sync wire format used by the closed-source Engram product. The inspected crate includes capture and retrieval helpers, embeddings, a write-through associative cache, and sync data types; this review does not measure product behavior or performance.

who_what.text: The repository identifies EL AI Intelligence, LLC in the README copyright and describes this repository as the open format and Rust crate behind a separate closed-source Engram product (daemon, relay, browser vault, and MCP servers). No individual maintainer identity is inferred.
The crate exposes a native SQLCipher storage feature and a pure format/browser WASM feature; it is a library and reference implementation, not the complete Engram service.

architecture.text: The code documents three layers: `QemCache` as an L1 associative cache, `EngramStore` as an encrypted SQLite/FTS5/vector store, and `ContextAssembler` as a token-budgeted retrieval layer. The README separately says the daemon and product interfaces are closed source, so this repository cannot establish their end-to-end behavior.

The reference vault stores engrams with content, capture context, layer/source, strength, valence, retrieval count, imagined/grounded flags, project, tags, scope, timestamps, privacy level, and optional agent identity. Related tables hold embeddings, links, evidence pairs, annotations, app metrics, tombstones, access events, and FTS5 search text.

The README and format specification describe SQLCipher encryption at rest and local key derivation. The specification distinguishes machine-ID-derived keys, which it says protect against offline disk cloning but not a local user, from passphrase vaults using Argon2id. These are design statements; this review did not independently cryptographically audit the implementation.

The README states crate version 0.1.4 in its usage example while the inspected Cargo manifest is 0.1.6; the FORMAT introduction says schema version 9 while its schema section and implementation identify version 10. The local implementation and documentation therefore have version drift.

behavior.text: `EngramStore::write` runs capture gates for episodic entries: noise filtering, normalized-content hash deduplication, and optional near-duplicate checks when an embedding is supplied. Duplicate captures strengthen an existing row; successful writes upsert the engram, synchronize FTS text, optionally store embeddings, and add carried or inferred links. `write_curated` bypasses the capture gates for reviewed changes.

The visible crate exposes upsert-style writes and curated rewrites; it does not expose a general-purpose patch API in the inspected public backend contract. `get` returns a memory by ID and touches retrieval counters/timestamps. FTS5 content search has a LIKE fallback for queries the FTS parser cannot handle; vector search is a separate path.

`delete` removes the engram and related indexed data and records a tombstone transactionally; `delete_without_tombstone` is a distinct lower-level option. The format describes tombstones as the mechanism preventing a deleted row from reappearing after sync, but this review did not exercise relay acknowledgment or deletion across devices.

The store includes daily strength/decay hygiene, weekly promotion/pruning, explicit relation lookup, FTS retrieval, vector similarity, and `surface_relevant` scoring. QEM uses 32-bit XOR codes for associative lookup and writes through to the persistent backend before caching; its code describes collisions as acceptable for a cache. No retrieval answers were evaluated.

The format records `project`, `scope`, privacy level, and agent identity, but the generic `Query` includes project and scope fields that the `EngramStoreAdapter::search` implementation does not apply: it dispatches only on layer, text, tags, or list. The adapter calls unfiltered store methods, whose default quarantine filter is `All`. Thus those fields do not provide enforced isolation through this generic search path.

The store schema has `memory_evidence` and `annotations` tables, and access events record a memory ID, operation, client, content hash, and time without storing memory text. However, `MemoryEntry::from(Engram)` initializes evidence to an empty vector, and the inspected generic contract does not load those evidence pairs into returned entries. Stored relations/provenance therefore should not be mistaken for citations attached to retrieved claims.

The QEM implementation keeps hit/miss counters and the store tracks capture-skip counters and access events. These are code-level instrumentation points; the inspected crate does not establish a surfaced monitoring dashboard, retention policy, or operational alerting behavior.

metrics.evidence: FTS, vector, and context-surface paths are present; no answers or abstentions were scored.
Upsert and curated-write paths exist; no correction sequence or stale-value rate was measured.
Local tombstone code is present; no post-delete recall probes or replica cleanup audit were performed.
Project/scope fields are represented, but the generic adapter omits those filters; no isolation workload was run.
Evidence relationships can be stored, but the adapter conversion drops them from MemoryEntry; no claim-evidence adjudication was done.
No runtime timing data was collected.
No workload, token, cost, or storage measurements were collected.

limits.text: This review inspected the public Rust crate and its format documentation, not the closed-source daemon, relay, MCP servers, or browser vault. It cannot establish how the product wires these components or enforces product-level controls.

The generic adapter's omitted project/scope filters and unfiltered default quarantine behavior are source observations for that path; callers may use other APIs. No application-level security or tenant-isolation conclusion is made beyond the inspected code.

Evidence tables and sync structures describe storage formats, not factual validity, source citation quality, encryption resistance to attacks, or correctness under crashes and multi-device conflict. Those properties were not experimentally verified.

The current repository head was verified, but GitHub REST API metadata requests returned HTTP 403 during review. The Git remote's advertised HEAD and shallow checkout agreed on branch `main` and full SHA; no API response was used as corroboration.

benchmark.note: No Engram Format system, tests, or benchmarks were run. Source inspection and format claims are not measured results.
